title: multi-signal eval orchestrator with progressive CI fallback
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a runtime-agnostic orchestrator that fuses multiple eval signals (accuracy, calibration drift, latency regressions, tokenization instability) and escalates with a progressive CI fallback plan to avoid noisy hard failures.
description:
Summary: This PR implements a multi-signal eval orchestrator and a progressive CI fallback policy for our eval-harness. Motivation: we've seen sporadic CI failures where a single brittle metric (e.g. a high-variance prompt cohort) caused full CI hard-fails and blocked rollouts. The orchestrator fuses orthogonal signals (cohort-level regression score, semantic-change distance, tokenization mismatch rate, and latency tail events) into a unified severity score and drives a graded CI response: soft-fail annotations -> targeted replay -> staggered quarantine -> hard-fail only if multiple independent signals cross thresholds.

What changed (high-level):
- New orchestrator core (eval_orchestrator.py) with plugin hooks for signal adapters and pluggable fusion strategies (median + rank aggregation, weighted voting).
- Signal adapters for: cohort_regression, semantic_embedding_delta, tokenization_jitter, latency_p99_delta. Each adapter emits a normalized severity float plus provenance metadata.
- CI hook (ci/fallback-scheduler.yaml + scripts/ci_fallback_runner.sh) that queries latest orchestrator decision and applies the progressive response (annotate, queue replay job, quarantine subset, escalate).
- Targeted replay runner that can execute a lightweight replay on a single model shard / seed set to reduce noise before failing the whole job.
- Telemetry: new metrics (eval.orchestrator.severity, eval.signal.*.score, eval.ci.fallback.action) and logging to the existing influx exporter with tags for model, prompt_set, cohort_id, and seed.
- Tests: unit coverage for fusion logic, adapters, and an integration smokeflow that simulates a flaky cohort and verifies the fallback ladder behavior.

Commits (summary):
- c1a3d9e: implement orchestrator core and plugin registry
- 7b2f90a: add cohort_regression and semantic_embedding_delta adapters
- d4f1a76: tokenization_jitter and latency adapters + normalization utils
- a9b8c12: CI fallback scheduler + runner scripts
- f3e5b21: telemetry hooks and metrics mapping
- 2c7b4d0: add unit and integration tests + test fixtures

Files touched (representative):
- eval_harness/orchestrator/eval_orchestrator.py
- eval_harness/adapters/cohort_regression.py
- eval_harness/adapters/semantic_delta.py
- eval_harness/adapters/tokenization_jitter.py
- eval_harness/adapters/latency_p99.py
- ci/fallback-scheduler.yaml
- scripts/ci_fallback_runner.sh
- tests/orchestrator/test_fusion.py
- tests/integration/test_progressive_fallback_sim.py

Testing & CI: Initial CI run hit a flaky integration smoke test (simulated cohort with nondeterministic seed replay) causing the job to show a partial failure. I added deterministic seeds and narrower time windows in the replay runner, retriggered CI, and the final run passed all checks: unit, lint, smoke-integration, e2e-replay. Coverage summary: new modules ~82% unit coverage; overall repo coverage unchanged.

Review thread (high level):
- Jonas Klein: asked for clearer separation between signal normalization and fusion weighting; requested an explicit docstring explaining the semantics of "severity". Author response: clarified normalization contract, and added a small doc in eval_orchestrator.py explaining assumptions and a recommended default weight matrix.
- Priya Menon: requested a low-risk default in CI (soft-fail/annotate) and an opt-in flag for stricter behavior. Author response: added `EVAL_CI_MODE` env var (soft|staggered|strict) with default "soft" and updated ci/fallback-scheduler.yaml.
- Luca Rossi: requested telemetry tags to include model_revision and cohort_anchor. Author response: added tags and a short migration note for dashboards.
- Code owner review: minor nits on logging levels fixed in subsequent commit. Final approvals by Jonas and Priya on 2026-02-02.

Backwards compatibility: Default behavior is non-breaking and conservative: CI defaults to annotate + queue replay. Operators can opt into stricter fallback via env flags. No public API changes to existing eval result schemas (adapter provenance is an additive field).

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind a boolean flag (EVAL_ORCHESTRATOR_ENABLED) in infra; we plan a staged rollout: 1) enable in canary CI pool for repo owners, 2) enable for internal teams (redwood-wide), 3) enable by default. Observability dashboards added to the Eval Overview board for the canary stage.

Related tickets: ENG-1428 (design doc), PM-337 (acceptance criteria), SUP-9082 (customer incident that motivated progressive fallback).

Merge: squash-and-merge after approvals and CI green.

Notes: This PR aims to reduce noisy CI churn while preserving early detection of substantive regressions. The fusion strategy is intentionally conservative; future work includes adaptive weighting based on historical signal reliability and an automated quarantine shrink/expand policy based on false-positive rates.
